test_title: PYST 30: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following accurately describes the Indian President's role in foreign affairs?

options.text: The President delegates all foreign affairs responsibilities to the Prime Minister.
The President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.
The President only receives foreign ambassadors but does not appoint them
The President is solely responsible for negotiating international treaties without any advisory input.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian President, as the head of state, exercises certain powers related to foreign affairs, including appointing ambassadors and conducting diplomatic actions in their name.
 
• All international treaties and agreements are signed in the name of the President, but they require ratification by Parliament to become binding.
 
• The President formally represents India in international forums and receives foreign ambassadors and dignitaries.
 
• While the President's role is largely ceremonial in foreign affairs, the Prime Minister and the Ministry of External Affairs handle the substantive and decision-making aspects.
 
• Constitutionally, the President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, in matters related to foreign policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ambassadors:**

 
 
• Ambassadors are official representatives of a nation in foreign countries.
 
• They are appointed by the President of India based on recommendations from the Ministry of External Affairs.
 
• Ambassadors play key roles in promoting diplomatic relations, trade, and cultural exchanges.
 
 
 
• **International Treaties:**
 
 
• International treaties signed by the President must be approved by Parliament under Article 253 of the Constitution.
 
• Treaties cover a wide range of subjects, including trade, defense, and environmental agreements.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Prime Minister:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister leads foreign policy decision-making in consultation with the Cabinet.
 
• While the President represents India ceremonially, the Prime Minister negotiates and shapes international relations.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of External Affairs:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for India's foreign relations, trade agreements, and diplomatic missions.
 
• It coordinates closely with the President and Prime Minister to implement India's foreign policy.
